topic: What link budget trade-offs arise when adjusting elevation angles and spatial filtering for dynamic power allocation in MSS?
consensus_response: Adjusting elevation angles for dynamic power allocation introduces trade-offs between interference suppression, admission control, and QoS guarantees. Spatial filtering impacts link budget trade-offs by altering the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and capacity allocation. Increasing elevation angles reduces sidelobes but decreases gain, while decreasing angles increases gain but raises sidelobes. This trade-off affects the array factor, impacting interference suppression and admission control in MSS. Dynamic power allocation strategies must consider the interplay between spatial filtering, interference suppression, and admission control to optimize link budget trade-offs.
reference_context: The reference context includes various studies on resource management for advanced transmission antenna satellites, QoS-provisioning in converged satellite and terrestrial networks, joint pricing and power allocation for multibeam satellite systems with dynamic game models, and a technical comparison of three low-Earth orbit satellite constellation systems. These studies highlight the importance of considering system parameters such as diameters, efficiencies, and noise temperatures of transmitter and receiver antennas when designing MSS systems.
